purpose: Independent mechanism search; user authorized ongoing T3 research.

tasks.title: Factoring: smoothness and relation mechanisms
tasks.lens: Explore relation generation and dependency extraction beyond standard QS/NFS: structured norm values, correlations among relations, partial smoothness, useful congruent squares, alternative factorizable representations. Carefully charge any density gain against relation generation, matrix size and dependence; distinguish L_N[alpha,c] exponent/constant improvement from small-input tricks.

tasks.title: Factoring: deterministic exponent mechanisms
tasks.lens: Explore deterministic factoring via product trees, multipoint evaluation, approximate divisors, rational approximations, and combinatorial collision coverage. Start from primary literature on improvements beyond N^(1/4), including Harvey/Hittmeir and newer work if found. Seek one concrete way to reduce a total exponent or logarithmic overhead, rather than relabel a known theorem.

tasks.title: Factoring: lifting, lattice and carry mechanisms
tasks.lens: Explore p-adic/2-adic lifting, multiplication carries, lattice small roots, constraint pruning and coordinate representations. Analyze whether compact representations of all lifts can support useful queries without exponential decoding. No known bits of the factors may be assumed unless their acquisition is priced. Give distinct mechanisms and cheap counterexamples to unjustified pruning.

tasks.title: Factoring: order finding and dequantization
tasks.lens: Explore classically accessible structure in modular exponentiation, order recovery, compressed Fourier/interference representations and dequantization restricted to factoring. Distinguish exact amplitudes, approximate sampling and recoverable classical periods. Any exponentially large state, hidden order, precision, low-rank assumption or tensor contraction must be priced. Seek concrete primitives, not a claim that generic quantum simulation is easy.

tasks.title: Factoring: algebraic zero-divisor mechanisms
tasks.lens: Explore polynomial rings over Z/NZ, resultants, class-group or algebraic invariants, rank defects, nontrivial idempotents, and efficient zero-divisor constructions. Identify any circularity in requiring the factorization to compute an invariant. Target representations that genuinely change arithmetic structure; include a concrete identity or lemma worth testing.

tasks.title: Factoring: collision and group-order mechanisms
tasks.lens: Explore collision search, nonuniform walks, batch gcd, ECM/group-order selection, p−1 variants and representation-specific dynamics. Can collisions modulo a hidden factor become more likely without equivalent work or loss of extraction probability? Price setup, orbit overlap, walk correlation and restarts. Distinguish known constant-factor gains from asymptotic gain.

tasks.title: Factoring: current primary-literature baseline
tasks.lens: Your report is a baseline ledger rather than 3–4 speculation cards: verify primary literature for general classical factoring, distinguishing heuristic GNFS, expected/proven randomized methods, deterministic worst-case exponents, special-factor methods, and actual quantum results. Search for relevant newer 2024–2026 work. Give exact assumptions, correct variable N versus log N, and 3 promising research bottlenecks supported by the sources. Flag unsupported novelty claims a reviewer should catch. Do not claim your survey exhaustive.
